answer: The example given in arXiv 2303.17558 to illustrate when a model is considered interpretable in financial decision-making is a system that predicts the likelihood of not being able to pay back a mortgage. It is considered interpretable only if it makes clear which financially significant factors—such as wage, job type, age, concurrent loans, marital status, and education—were used by the model to produce the output, what relationships were found between them, and which ones were given a higher weight than others.
